title: TideScale - marketplace listing & on-prem preview
summary: Redwood + TideScale alignment on marketplace listing checklist and preview of on-prem connector. Discussed packaging, installer bits, KMS/HSM integration, network topology, and a short compatibility matrix. Agreed next steps: run on-prem compatibility test, provide listing artifact bundle, and share SOC2 docs. SE to validate kernel/quantization compatibility with TideScale GPU nodes.
next_steps: Redwood: share marketplace artifact bundle + listing checklist by 2026-08-07
TideScale: provide access to test cluster images by 2026-08-10
SEs: schedule on-prem compatibility run week of 2026-08-10
Sales: update deal record with preflight items
action_items: Priya Kapoor - run quantized model inference on TideScale node and report perf delta - due 2026-08-14
Maya Gomez - prepare listing artifact bundle (helm chart, manifest, quickstart) and upload to shared S3 - due 2026-08-07
Evan Park - share a small test VPC config and an AMI/OCI image reference - due 2026-08-10
Amira Hassan - confirm KMS/HSM certs and audit log retention requirements - due 2026-08-12
transcript:
[00:00] Jasper Liu: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Jasper from Redwood... um I think we have Priya and Maya on the call too. Can you see my screen?
[00:08] Nora Singh: Yep seeing it, thanks. We're Nora, Liam, Amira and Evan on the TideScale side. Appreciate you making time.
[00:14] Jasper Liu: Great. Quick agenda: listing checklist for the marketplace, a preview of the on-prem connector packaging, and then an open Q&A about security and network constraints. We'll try to keep the deep kernel stuff for the SE section.
[00:26] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Our timeline is tight — marketing wants the listing live by end of August. We're flexible on staging but need the on-prem preview asap.
[00:34] Priya Kapoor: Great — we'll aim to split deliverables. I'll cover runtime/compatibility and Maya will cover packaging and the listing artifact.
[00:39] Maya Gomez: Hi all. Big picture — the listing needs a few pieces: a validated helm chart, quickstart, sample policy for RBAC/SAML, and the billing/metering hooks. We also recommend a small reference arch doc for VPC and on-prem.
[00:50] Evan Park: On billing hooks — TideScale has a meter agent that collects usage; do you have a preferred metrics endpoint or pull model?
[00:58] Jasper Liu: We usually support both. For marketplace listings we accept a pull-friendly Prometheus endpoint and a push webhook. For private deployments customers often prefer local metering with logs forwarded to our billing converter.
[01:09] Amira Hassan: Security first question: the customer data residency and KMS integration. Our security team requires HSM-backed encryption for all customer keys. Is Redwood's private deployment compatible with external HSM/KMS?
[01:22] Priya Kapoor: Short answer yes. We support KMS integrations via standard KMIP and cloud KMS APIs. For HSM we have an on-prem connector that can integrate with customer HSMs; you'll need to expose the credential endpoint and service CIDR so the connector can reach the HSM. We'll share a reference flow.
[01:36] Nora Singh: When you say 'connector', is that a separate pod or baked into the runtime image? Curious about upgrade surface.
[01:44] Maya Gomez: It's a sidecar pattern in our current helm chart — keeps runtime image small and allows you to swap vault/HSM implementations without rebuilding the model runtime.
[01:52] Liam O'Connor: That helps. For our environment, networking is stricter — no outbound to public endpoints from the worker nodes. Does Redwood require egress for telemetry or model downloads?
[02:02] Priya Kapoor: For hosted deployments yes, but for Private we can operate fully offline. The listing flow expects a staged bundle — pre-pulled images and an offline installer. For telemetry you can opt into local sink only; we can also ship logs to your SIEM via a forwarder.
[02:18] Jasper Liu: That offline installer is what we'll demo today in preview. Priya, do you want to take them through the compatibility matrix?
[02:24] Priya Kapoor: Sure. I'll share screen. (brief pause) Our main compatibility vectors are GPU driver version (CUDA 11 vs 12), libc/GLIBC baseline, and kernel config for improved attention kernels. Also quantization format: we support int8 and 4-bit variants, but some vendor-specific kernels on older GPUs have lower perf.
[02:41] Evan Park: Our nodes run CUDA 11.8 and an RKernels build that had some unusual kernel flags, we've seen perf regressions on other runtimes.
[02:50] Priya Kapoor: Okay noted. The quick test we'll run is: 1) pull the RB image, 2) run a short inference job with a 2k token context, 3) measure throughput and peak memory. If you can provide a node to test, I'll run the quantized vs fp16 baseline and report.
[03:06] Nora Singh: That test is acceptable. We'll need guidance on expected numbers — like baseline latency at 2k tokens so our infra team has something to compare.
[03:14] Priya Kapoor: We'll provide expected ranges. For example on an A40-ish node we expect ~X tokens/sec for the model family you mentioned — sorry the model name got jumbled earlier, what model are you planning to host?
[03:24] Liam O'Connor: We're looking at the big open family, 'SeaStorm-XL' — we tested it lightly.
[03:29] Priya Kapoor: Right SeaStorm — sometimes transcribed as Seastorm. For SeaStorm-XL on A40 with our runtime and fp16 you'd see roughly 12-18 tokens/sec depending on batch and KV cache behaviour. Quantized to int8 maybe 1.3-1.5x perf change but that can vary.
[03:43] Jasper Liu: Important to call out: caching strategy (prefix vs full KV cache) will change your memory profile. We'll send a sample config that demonstrates continuous batching and the tradeoffs.
[03:52] Amira Hassan: Audit logs — what retention and format do you ship? We need to map to our SIEM and keep raw audit trails for 1 year for compliance.
[04:00] Maya Gomez: The private deployment ships audit logs in JSONL; you can set retention or forward to your SIEM. For the marketplace listing we recommend including a short 'security considerations' doc that states defaults and where to configure retention.
[04:10] Nora Singh: For listing metadata, are there required fields for the marketplace? e.g., support contacts, SLAs, verbiage about private deployments?
[04:17] Jasper Liu: Yes the marketplace requires: listing summary, technical requirements, support contact, region availability, a small user guide, and a 'known limitations' section. We'll send a checklist. Maya, that'll be part of your artifact.
[04:28] Maya Gomez: Yep. We'll include a sample support matrix and a default SLA clause.
[04:31] Liam O'Connor: On upgrades: if we install via the helm chart, can we pin the runtime version and opt for canary rollouts across clusters?
[04:38] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely — our charts include annotations for canary and can roll across node pools. We also have automatic fallback to a lighter-weight model if we detect errors during rollouts.
[04:48] Evan Park: About the lighter-weight model — is that a Redwood hosted artifact or something customers must provide?
[04:53] Jasper Liu: We can provide compatible model fallbacks as part of the package — or you can bring your own licensed model. We'll document tradeoffs in the listing docs.
[04:59] Nora Singh: Security follow-up: we need to validate that telemetry endpoints are optional and that no PII is sent back by default.
[05:06] Priya Kapoor: Telemetry is opt-in. The default private chart disables outbound telemetry. The only thing we request during listing is a clear explanation that the product supports both online and offline modes.
[05:15] Liam O'Connor: Can we get the SOC2 docs?
[05:18] Jasper Liu: Yes — we'll attach SOC2 + ISO attestation as part of the partner preflight bundle. We'll also include our third-party pen test summary redacted.
[05:27] Amira Hassan: Great. Network question: TideScale requires the ability to NAT some egress through a jumpbox. Any constraints on IP whitelisting for the installer?
[05:35] Maya Gomez: For the offline installer you won't need egress. For occasional checks we can accept a list of IPs to whitelist or provide a signed bundle. The packaging supports both approaches.
[05:43] Jasper Liu: Quick demo note — the preview we're doing today will show the offline installer deploy in a local K8s cluster. Priya, can you talk about the runtime hooks real quick?
[05:51] Priya Kapoor: Sure. The runtime exposes lifecycle hooks for model download, KV cache priming, and health check endpoints. We added an init container that primes the KV cache if you opt-in, which helps cold-starts for long contexts. Some of that naming gets transcribed weirdly — it's K-V cache, not K-V cash — apologies for earlier.
[06:07] Nora Singh: hah, noted. Small thing but important.
[06:10] Jasper Liu: Let's move to planning tests. We'll need: 1) TideScale to give a test node/image, 2) Redwood SE to run quantized vs fp16, 3) produce a short perf report, 4) Maya packages the chart and documentation. Agreed?
[06:22] Evan Park: Agreed. We'll provision an instance for you.
[06:24] Nora Singh: Should we schedule a follow-up in two weeks to review results?
[06:28] Jasper Liu: Yes — propose 2026-08-19 same time?
[06:31] Liam O'Connor: Works for us.
[06:33] Jasper Liu: Cool. A few clarifications from the SE track before we close — Priya?
[06:37] Priya Kapoor: One more technical caveat: if you plan to enable 4-bit quant on older kernels you might see correctness differences on attention ops. We'll run a validation suite that includes a small regression test harness to spot divergences. We'll include the harness in the artifact.
[06:52] Amira Hassan: Can that harness be run by our security team on the cluster? They prefer running tests in their environment before we open the cluster to partners.
[06:58] Priya Kapoor: Yes it's self-contained and runs offline. We'll include a README with required inputs.
[07:04] Maya Gomez: I'll add the harness link into the shared artifact bucket. Link: https://s3.redwood.example/partners/tidescale/refarch/harness (placeholder).
[07:12] Nora Singh: Nice. Anything else on marketplace metadata?
[07:16] Jasper Liu: We should cover region availability — TideScale, do you plan to offer in APAC and EMEA initially, or just NA?
[07:23] Liam O'Connor: NA first, EMEA next quarter, APAC later in the year.
[07:29] Jasper Liu: Ok we'll reflect that in the listing metadata.
[07:32] Evan Park: One small question: are there templated liability terms for the marketplace listing or is it custom per partner?
[07:38] Maya Gomez: There's a standard template but customers can add partner-specific clauses. We'll share the template with the legal redlines highlighted.
[07:45] Amira Hassan: Please send the SOC2 and the legal template to amira@tidescale.example.
[07:50] Jasper Liu: Noted. We'll attach in the follow-up.
[07:53] (Brief silence, typing)
[08:00] Jasper Liu: Ok I think that's the core of it. Recap: Redwood to share artifact bundle and SOC2 by 2026-08-07; TideScale to provide test node/image by 2026-08-10; SE to run compatibility tests and share perf report by 2026-08-14; follow-up scheduled for 2026-08-19.
[08:20] Nora Singh: That captures it, thanks everyone.
[08:23] Liam O'Connor: Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic plan.
[08:26] Priya Kapoor: Thanks all. We'll ping in the shared channel.
[08:29] Jasper Liu: Thanks folks — meeting adjourned.
[08:31] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings of model names (SeaStorm transcribed as Seastorm in chat), and 'KV cache' was at one point mis-transcribed as 'K-V cash' in earlier automated portion. Shared artifacts referenced: marketplace checklist (link to internal GDrive), helm chart preview (s3 link placeholder), performance harness (s3 link placeholder).
